description: Turn settlement and argument coercion (design A1 + A2; plan.md items 1-6). The root cause of stall 1 is that WriteToFileTool.execute calls newContent.startsWith on an object content outside its try. BaseTool.handle, executeAssistantMessageBlock and presentAssistantMessage do not catch it, and presentAssistantMessageSafe logs and drops it, so userMessageContentReady never flips and the pWaitFor at Task.ts ~4227 hangs forever. This feature adds a dispatch try/catch in the presenter (tool + MCP), a Task backstop (recoverFromPresenterFailure) and a stream-end guard, coercion of object/array write_to_file.content and update_todo_list.todos in NativeToolCallParser (partial + final), and a WriteToFileTool non-string guard. It also records the round-3 review responses in design.md first, so later FEATs read a consistent design. It is the foundation for FEAT-003/FEAT-004: FEAT-004's nudge reuses the hoisted telemetryToolName and sits inside this try.

Remove the inner `const isCustomTool` (~730), and use telemetryToolName in the validation catch (~766) and as recordName (~777). Wrap from '// Check for identical consecutive tool calls.' The catch, in order: (1) rethrow if cline.abort or the Error message ends with 'aborted'; (2) return on AskIgnoredError; (3) if block.partial, console.warn and return (no result); (4) normalize to Error, console.error with the task id and tool name, consecutiveMistakeCount++, recordToolError(telemetryToolName, msg), didToolFailInCurrentTurn = true, await handleError(`executing ${block.name}`, err). plan.md item 3: in src/core/task/Task.ts, presentAssistantMessageSafe (~485) calls `this.recoverFromPresenterFailure(error)` after the console.error in the non-abort branch. Add `private recoverFromPresenterFailure(error: unknown): void`: (1) return if this.abort || this.abandoned; (2) console.warn and return if presentAssistantMessageLocked; (3) push one is_error tool_result (formatResponse.toolError(`Tool execution failed unexpectedly: ${message}. Fix the arguments and retry.`), tool_use_id = sanitizeToolUseId(id)) for every tool_use/mcp_tool_use block with an id from currentStreamingContentIndex onward that has no result yet (partial blocks included); (4) set currentStreamingContentIndex = assistantMessageContent.length and presentAssistantMessageHasPendingUpdates = false; (5) if didCompleteReadingStream, set userMessageContentReady = true; (6) `void this.say('error', t('common:errors.presenter_failed', { message })).catch(...)`. Never write presentAssistantMessageLocked. Add the stream-end guard right before the pWaitFor at ~4227: `if (!this.presentAssistantMessageLocked && this.currentStreamingContentIndex >= this.assistantMessageContent.length) this.userMessageContentReady = true`.

Presenter try/catch boundaries: (1) tool_use: `try {` opens at the comment '// Any throw from dispatch must still answer this tool_use, or the turn never settles.' just before '// Check for identical consecutive tool calls.' (~815). It closes after the end of `switch (block.name)` with `} catch (error) {` (~1123). The repetition check (FEAT-004's nudge site) is INSIDE this try. (2) mcp_tool_use: the same comment + `try {` (~375) wraps the server-name resolution through `await useMcpToolTool.handle(...)`. DEVIATION (test expectation change): two existing cases in presentAssistantMessage-unknown-tool.spec.ts ('does not continue after queued denial persistence fails', 'does not execute an approved tool when queued approval persistence fails') asserted that presentAssistantMessage REJECTS with 'Failed to persist queued approval feedback …' and that userMessageContent stays []. Per the approved design (A error table: 'Tool dispatch | Any throw (non-abort) | is_error tool_result + chat error row'), the new catch answers it instead. Before this change the rejection was logged and dropped by presentAssistantMessageSafe, so the turn hung. The tests now assert that the presenter resolves, the tool still does not continue, no user_feedback row is posted, and exactly one tool_result containing the persistence error is pushed. The plan said those specs would be 'unchanged'; that was wrong for these two cases.
